title: theme tokens (CSS variables)
description: `ui/src/theme` is the only source of colour, spacing, radius and type tokens for the Tauri/React app, exposed as CSS variables and Tailwind CSS 4 `@theme` tokens. Tokens: surface/raised/overlay, border, text primary/secondary/muted, accent, success/warning/danger, focus ring; spacing 2/4/8/12/16/24/32; radii 3/6/10; type sizes 11/12/13/15/18/22 with Inter for UI and Menlo for mono. Dark is default; light uses the same token names. Public API: typed `ThemeTokens` plus `applyTheme(root, mode)`.
acceptance: `ThemeTokens.dark` and `ThemeTokens.light` expose identical key sets; a unit test fails if any key is missing in either theme.
No raw hex colours or font-size literals exist outside `ui/src/theme`; a CI grep check fails the build when one appears.
Switching theme at runtime re-themes shell, tables and overlays with no restart and no clipped labels at 1x and 2x.
Text-on-surface contrast is >= 4.5:1 for every pair, asserted by a unit test over the token table.
notes: Tokens mirror the FigCraft design-system page; TU-001..TU-005 are cross-cutting UI foundation with no single product epic, filed under E10.

title: component library (button, badge, chip, toggle, checkbox, input, segmented, radio card, status dot)
description: Implement the shared widgets in `ui/src/components`: button (primary, secondary, ghost, destructive), badge, chip/filter chip, toggle, checkbox, single-line input, segmented control, radio card and status dot. Each is a React component built on Radix UI primitives and styled with Tailwind CSS 4 (shadcn/ui pattern), controlled through props and typed callbacks; no widget keeps global state. Status dot and badge must express Linked, Off, Native, Conflict, Drifted, Locked and Shadowed.
acceptance: Every widget renders default, hover, active, focused and disabled states in a gallery window; destructive variants are covered too.
Item states use colour plus a text label or glyph, never colour alone; a test asserts each state has a non-colour marker.
All controls are Tab-reachable and activate on Space/Enter; the focus ring is visible on the dark theme at 1x and 2x.
A widget never mutates model data directly; it returns the interaction result and the caller applies it.
notes: Used by the shell, tables, forms and preferences; states map to at-model ItemState.

title: table component (virtualized, sortable, per-agent cells)
description: `ui/src/components/table` wraps TanStack Table and TanStack Virtual for virtualized lists with sortable headers, row menu hook, selection model and a per-agent cell renderer. The cell renderer covers linked toggle, off, native-with-path tooltip, none, locked and shadowed. Used by Skills, MCP Servers and Effective config lists.
acceptance: 5,000 rows with 4 agent columns render at 60 fps on the reference Mac; only visible rows are laid out, asserted by an instrumentation counter.
Clicking a header sorts by that column, keeps selection and is stable for equal keys.
Selection supports single click, Cmd-click toggle and Shift-range; Select all applies to filtered rows only and shows the correct count.
A per-agent cell renders each of the six states with the correct widget and tooltip; a snapshot covers all six.
Empty and loading states delegate to the TU-021 `StateView` without layout shift.
notes: Column widths persist through TU-018.

title: modal/popover/menu framework
description: `ui/src/components/overlay` provides modal, popover and menu containers with a stack, backdrop, focus trap, Esc handling and typed results. Callers get `ModalResult<T>` (Confirmed(T), Cancelled, Dismissed) instead of reading shared flags. Popovers anchor to a widget rect and clamp inside the window.
acceptance: Overlays stack; Esc closes only the topmost; click-outside closes popovers but not destructive modals.
Opening a modal moves focus inside, Tab cycles within it, and closing restores focus to the opener widget.
Menus support disabled items with a reason tooltip, separators, mnemonics and Up/Down/Enter navigation.
Popovers reposition when the anchor scrolls or the window resizes and never render outside the viewport.

title: toast service
description: `ui/src/overlays/toasts` provides a toast queue rendered in the top layer: success, warning, info and error kinds, optional action button, auto-dismiss after 2.5 s. Errors never auto-dismiss. The service is owned by `AppState` and driven by a testable clock.
acceptance: At most 3 toasts are visible; extra toasts wait in FIFO order; each auto-dismisses after 2.5 s measured with an injected clock.
Error toasts stay until closed and expose Copy details; a second identical toast within 1 s collapses into one with a count badge.
Toasts render bottom-right above the status bar and never cover the primary action of the active screen.
Toast text is exposed to the accessibility tree as a live region (see TU-022).

title: app shell (sidebar, top bar, routing)
description: `ui/src/shell` `Shell` component draws the permanent chrome: sidebar with logo, nav sections Overview, Skills, MCP Servers, Instructions, Agents, Effective config, Sync & drift, plus agents-on-this-Mac and account blocks; top bar with project picker trigger, scope switcher, palette hint and window title. The shell hosts the routed screen body and all overlay layers.
acceptance: Sidebar renders every F01 section with icon and label; the active route is highlighted and updates on navigation.
Top bar hosts the project picker trigger, TU-040 scope switcher and Cmd+K palette hint; layout stays usable at 900 px width with no overlapping controls.
The shell renders loading, empty, error and populated child states without layout shift.
Sidebar and top bar remain keyboard reachable and expose ARIA roles and names (see TU-022).
notes: Routing behaviour is TU-010; this story owns the chrome only.

title: diff viewer component
description: `ui/src/components/diff` renders unified and side-by-side diffs from `similar::TextDiff` with line numbers, change counts, syntax highlighting via CodeMirror 6 (@codemirror/merge) and a Copy diff action. Used by write previews, migration conflicts and drift screens.
acceptance: Unified and side-by-side modes render from the same diff model with line numbers on both sides and +/- counts in the header.
Added and removed lines use distinct background tokens plus a textual marker, in both dark and light themes.
Files over 2 MB or 20k lines render truncated with a notice and Copy diff instead of blocking the UI.
Whitespace-only changes can be hidden with a toggle that updates the counts.

title: code/markdown editor component
description: `ui/src/components/editor` provides a text editor with line numbers, current-line highlight, markdown syntax highlighting (CodeMirror 6), Edit/Preview toggle (react-markdown), dirty tracking and a caller-supplied save callback wired to Cmd+S. Used by skill detail and instructions screens.
acceptance: Line numbers, current-line highlight, markdown highlighting and Edit/Preview toggle render for a 2,000-line file.
Dirty state compares against loaded text; the tab shows a dot and Cmd+S invokes the save callback with the current buffer.
Undo/redo covers typing, paste and programmatic edits with a bounded history.
Unreadable or malformed UTF-8 input shows an error state and keeps the editor read-only, without losing the previous buffer.
Wrap toggle works and horizontal scrolling keeps the caret visible.

title: app state store
description: `ui/src/state` `AppState` is the single source of truth for presentation state: active project, current scope as received from TA-053, route stack, per-screen view state, selection sets, editor buffers, overlay state and background job handles. Screens read `AppState` through hooks plus read-only snapshots fetched from Rust commands; no module-level mutable globals. Project and scope changes emit typed effects consumed by the bridge. The last project persists as the TF-023 `last_project_id` setting.
acceptance: All UI state lives in `AppState`; a grep test fails on `static mut`, `thread_local!` caches or screen-owned global data.
Switching project clears project-scoped caches and triggers exactly one reload of the current route (asserted by job count in a headless test).
Scope changes arrive as events from TA-053 and trigger exactly one reload of the current screen; AppState does not own scope persistence.
Navigating away from a dirty editor prompts Save/Discard/Cancel; Cancel aborts navigation and keeps the route and buffer.
`last_project_id` persists through TF-023 and sidebar expansion through window state (TU-018); both are restored before first paint.
notes: Headless tests construct AppState without a window.

title: routing, back stack and deep links
description: `ui/src/shell` `Route` is a TypeScript union with stable string ids: overview, skills, skill detail, mcp list/detail/form, effective, drift, instructions, agents, add skill, migrate, settings. The router keeps a bounded back stack, maps deep links to routes, and resolves item ids through at-db before rendering a detail screen.
acceptance: Every defined route renders and has a stable id string; a test round-trips ids through parse/display.
Back pops the stack on the Back button, Cmd+[ and Esc when no overlay is open; the stack is capped at 50 entries.
`agentuna://item/<item-id>` opens the matching detail screen after load; an unknown or deleted id shows `Item not found` toast and stays on the previous route.
Navigating to a project-scoped route with no active project opens the project picker instead of an empty screen.
notes: URL scheme registration is macOS packaging work; this story owns parsing and dispatch.

title: project registry DB queries
description: Extend the `projects` table repository in at-db: canonical path unique index, display name, source root, last_used_at, hidden flag. Provide list with per-project skill/server/rule counts in one query, touch, add, hide and lookup by path or id. Counts derive from `items` and `deployments` filtered by project scope.
acceptance: Migration adds a unique index on canonical path; inserting the same folder twice, including through a symlink, resolves to one row (test covers symlinked path).
`list_projects` returns path, name, last_used_at, skill_count, server_count and rule_count ordered by last_used_at desc then name, using one query with no per-row queries.
`touch_project` updates last_used_at only on selection change; `hide_project` leaves deployments and history rows intact.
Repository tests run against a temp SQLite DB and cover empty, duplicate and hidden cases.
notes: Counts are read-only projections; no denormalised counters in v1.

title: project detection scan
description: Project discovery in at-store: walk configured roots (default `~/Projects` plus user-added folders) to a bounded depth, treat a folder as a project when it contains `.git`, `.agentuna`, `.claude`, `.agents` or `.mcp.json`, skip heavy directories, and return a diff (new, missing, unchanged) for the DB upsert. Runs on a tokio task and reports progress.
acceptance: A fixture tree with repos nested 3 levels deep yields exactly the expected project set; `node_modules`, `target`, `.venv`, `dist` and ordinary hidden directories are skipped.
Duplicate detections (nested repos) collapse to the shallowest match; symlinked roots do not recurse into a cycle.
Permission-denied directories, missing roots and unreadable files become warnings in the result and never abort the scan.
The scan is cancellable, emits progress every 100 entries and applying its diff never changes last_used_at on existing projects.
notes: Detection lives in at-store rather than at-engine because it only reads the filesystem and produces registry rows.

title: project picker overlay with search highlight and keyboard
description: `ui/src/overlays/project_picker` renders a searchable, scrollable project list: name, abbreviated path, skill/server counts and relative last-used time. Footer has Add project folder (native folder dialog) and Scan ~/Projects. Search filters name and path and highlights matched spans. Full keyboard operation and loading, scanning, empty, no-results, error and populated states.
acceptance: Populated state lists all registered projects, virtualizes scrolling to 10k rows, and shows counts and last-used values from TU-011.
Typing filters on name and path; matched character spans are highlighted in both; no match shows `No projects match` with a Clear action.
Keyboard: Up/Down move, Enter activates and closes, Esc closes, Cmd+Enter reveals the folder in Finder; focus starts in the search field on open.
Loading shows skeleton rows, scan shows a progress row with cancel, and a permission-denied root shows an inline warning row with Retry.
Add folder on an already registered path selects the existing row instead of creating a duplicate; unreadable folder shows an inline error and leaves the list unchanged.

title: command palette index and fuzzy search
description: `ui/src/overlays/palette::index` builds a searchable inventory of skills, MCP servers, rule files, agents and actions from AppState plus at-db snapshots. Each entry has a stable id, kind, title, subtitle, keywords and a run handler. The matcher is case-insensitive subsequence with word-start and consecutive-run bonuses; results cap at 50 per kind group.
acceptance: Index contains one entry per skill, server, rule file, installed or known agent and registered action; ids are stable across reloads.
Query `mc` ranks the MCP Servers action and MCP server entries above unrelated matches; exact prefix beats word-boundary beats plain subsequence in fixture tests.
Empty query returns the last 8 visited items plus the top 6 actions; an empty index shows the action group only.
Searching 10,000 entries returns the top 50 in under 8 ms on the reference Mac, measured by a criterion bench.
The index invalidates on item version change, project switch and scope change; stale entries never appear after invalidation.
notes: Pure functions plus a cache; no UI painting in this story.

title: command palette overlay and action registry
description: `ui/src/overlays/palette` renders the Cmd+K overlay: query field, grouped results with icons and keyboard hints, highlighted matched spans, disabled actions with a reason, and a status line. The action registry holds run handlers for navigation, add flows, rescan, install CLI, preferences and item actions. States: idle with recents, typing with results, no results, loading while the index builds, error when the index fails.
acceptance: Cmd+K opens the palette, focuses the query field and paints within one frame; Esc closes and restores focus to the previous widget.
Results are grouped by kind with headers, show shortcut hints and bold matched spans; Up/Down/Home/End navigate, Enter runs, Cmd+Enter opens in the background.
No results shows `No matches` plus the three nearest actions; a failed index build shows an error state with Retry.
Actions that cannot run are disabled with a visible reason (locked, no project, agent missing); running one closes the palette and toasts its outcome.
Running any action is recorded with its id in the operations log through the same path as its button equivalent.

title: global keyboard shortcuts
description: Central `ui/src/shell` `ShortcutMap` maps platform keys to actions: Cmd+K palette, Cmd+P project picker, Cmd+S save active editor, Cmd+N add menu, Cmd+, preferences, Cmd+1..7 screen navigation, Cmd+Shift+1/2/3/4 scope selection (Global/User/Project/Local), Esc close topmost overlay. Dispatch runs after overlay input and honours text-focus rules. A Help > Keyboard Shortcuts sheet is generated from the map.
acceptance: The map and the generated sheet match: Cmd+1..7 screens, Cmd+Shift+1/2/3/4 scopes, Cmd+K palette, Cmd+P project picker, Cmd+S save, Cmd+N add menu, Cmd+, preferences and Esc close topmost overlay.
Cmd+S saves only the focused editor; with no editor focused it shows `Nothing to save` and creates no file.
Esc closes exactly one overlay per press and does nothing when no overlay is open, so it never leaves the current screen.
Cmd shortcuts still work while a text field has focus, except when the field consumed the key; plain-key shortcuts do not fire while typing.
Vitest + Testing Library keyboard-event tests cover overlay-open, editor-focused, plain-screen and each Cmd+Shift scope shortcut.

title: native macOS menu bar via muda
description: Build the native menu bar with muda at app start: App (About, Preferences Cmd+,, Quit), File (Add Skill, Add MCP Server, Add Rule File, Import), Edit (undo/redo/cut/copy/paste), View (one item per screen), Window, Help (Keyboard Shortcuts, Documentation, Run Doctor). Items dispatch the same action ids as the in-app UI.
acceptance: Every menu item dispatches an action id handled by the shared dispatcher; no menu item contains its own business logic.
Preferences opens `ui/src/screens/settings` and Help > Run Doctor shows a copyable report dialog.
Item enablement follows app state each frame (for example Add Skill is disabled while a modal owns focus) without rebuilding the native menu.
About states `No account, no telemetry` and the app version; there is no sign-in item.
Menu construction compiles on macOS and is compilable behind a no-op stub on Windows/Linux.
notes: Tauri's menu API (muda) runs on the main thread; menu events arrive through Tauri's menu-event handler and dispatch the same commands the webview uses.

title: window state persistence
description: Persist window size, position, monitor, maximized state, sidebar width and table column widths through a Rust command backed by the Tauri window-state store; restore before first paint and clamp to the visible display. Provide a Reset Window Layout command in Preferences.
acceptance: Restart restores window geometry within 2 px, maximized state and sidebar width.
If the saved monitor is disconnected, the window centers on the primary display and stays fully visible.
Corrupt or out-of-range stored values fall back to 1280x800 centered with a warning log and do not panic.
Reset Window Layout restores defaults immediately without restart and persists them.

title: Preferences screen
description: `ui/src/screens/settings` renders sections General (default link mode and per-agent link mode, native banner un-hide), Health (health interval and background health), Backups (retention days), Network (marketplace toggle and policy state), Storage (read-only global store path) and Reset. Every edit goes through TF-023, which owns the keys, types and validation. Each section has loading, first-run empty, error and populated states, inline validation and save toasts.
acceptance: All four states render for every section from fixtures; first run shows the TF-023 defaults: `health_interval_minutes=5`, `background_health=local`, `backup_retention_days=30`, `default_link_mode=link`, `network.marketplace_enabled=false`, and `global_store_path` resolved by TF-022 AppPaths.

General edits `default_link_mode` (link|copy) and per-agent `link_mode.<agent>`; when the target cannot create symlinks the link option is disabled with that reason and copy stays selected. Native banner rows can be un-hidden per kind, clearing `native_banner_hidden.<kind>`.

Health edits `health_interval_minutes` (off/5/15/60) and `background_health` (off/local/all, where local means stdio servers already tested once and HTTP requires all); Backups edits `backup_retention_days` with minimum 30 and rejects smaller values.

Network shows `network.marketplace_enabled` on/off plus the read-only policy statement that no automatic network call occurs and that offline mode disables network actions; Storage shows the read-only `global_store_path`.
Invalid input shows an inline error, writes nothing and keeps the stored value; valid changes persist through TF-023 with a success toast; a failed write shows a retryable error.
notes: Settings keys, defaults and validation are fixed by CONTRACT decision 9; TF-023 owns storage.

title: loading, empty and error state pattern
description: `ui/src/components/state` provides `StateView` with Loading, Empty, Error and Offline variants: title, body, primary action, optional secondary action, expandable details. Screens map domain errors (permission denied, malformed file, missing agent, conflict, offline, unknown) to human copy while keeping the raw path and OS error in details.
acceptance: Snapshot matrix covers every TU-010 route (overview, skills, skill detail, mcp list, mcp detail, mcp form, effective, drift, instructions, agents, add skill, migrate, settings) in all four variants: empty, loading, error and populated, at 1x and 2x. That is 13 routes x 4 variants x 2 scales = 104 goldens, plus shell and overlay states.
Empty shows one primary action and no stale rows; loading shows skeleton rows or a spinner with a label; populated renders fixture data through the real screen widget.
Error shows human copy with the raw path and OS error in expandable, copyable details, collapsed by default.
Retry re-runs the failed job through `app::bridge`, shows a spinner and keeps the previous error visible until the new result arrives.
A fixture test asserts every route id from TU-010 has all four variants and fails on a missing combination.

title: accessibility labels and focus order
description: Apply ARIA semantics across the shell and shared widgets: labels and roles on sidebar items, top bar controls, scope switcher, tables, toggles, overlays and toasts. Define a logical focus order, trap focus in modals, announce toast text, and ensure states are not conveyed by colour alone.
acceptance: A test runs axe-core against each screen's rendered DOM and fails on any button, toggle, text field or table cell without a label or role.
Toggles announce item, agent and state (`skill X, Claude Code, enabled`); locked, shadowed and native states appear in the label.
Sidebar, scope switcher and tables expose ordered focus targets; modal opening traps focus and removes background widgets from the tree.
Toasts are announced as a live region without moving focus, and no information is colour-only.
Text contrast remains >= 4.5:1 after adding accessibility styling.
notes: Radix primitives supply ARIA behaviour; axe-core is a dev dependency used only in tests.

title: keyboard-only flows and VoiceOver smoke test
description: A release-gating accessibility test pack: scripted keyboard-only flows plus a VoiceOver smoke session. Flows: switch project, switch scope, enable a skill for one agent, open a server detail, create a rule file, open the palette and run an action. Each step records keystrokes, expected focus and observed result.
acceptance: Every listed flow completes with keyboard only; each step records keystrokes and expected focus in a pass/fail table.
A 15-minute VoiceOver script verifies sidebar, scope switcher, per-agent toggles, table headers, palette and dialogs; results are attached to the release checklist.
Any step requiring a pointer is filed as a defect naming the widget and screen, not waived.
The pack runs on macOS 14+ with VoiceOver enabled and with the app built from the release profile.
notes: Manual VoiceOver steps are unavoidable; the keyboard flows are scripted with Playwright keyboard events.

title: HiDPI and font loading with fallbacks
description: Embed Inter (UI, 400/500/600) and Menlo (mono) in the app bundle and load them at startup with fallbacks to Helvetica/SF and `ui-monospace`. Handle pixels_per_point at 1x, 1.5x and 2x, monitor changes, and a user font-scale setting. Missing font files must not prevent launch.
acceptance: Missing font files fall back to system fonts with one warning log; the app still starts and renders all screens.
pixels_per_point is applied at startup and on monitor change; 1x, 1.5x and 2x screenshots show no clipped or overlapping labels.
Font scale 90/100/110/125% scales every token and persists through restart.
A 2x snapshot shows aligned monospace columns in the editor and table and no fractional-pixel blur on text.
notes: Font licensing: Inter and Menlo are bundled under their respective licences; record attribution in the About panel.

title: visual regression snapshot tests with Playwright
description: Build a Playwright harness that serves the built frontend with mocked Tauri IPC (`@tauri-apps/api/mocks`) and renders the shell, six representative screens and four overlays in populated, empty and error states at 1x and 2x, with deterministic fixtures and a frozen clock. Compare against golden PNGs and publish diff images on failure.
acceptance: At least 12 snapshots cover shell, skills, MCP list, effective config, project picker, palette, preferences and the shared state views at 1x and 2x.
A pixel diff over 0.1% fails the test and writes a side-by-side diff image as a CI artifact.
`UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p at-app --test snapshots` regenerates goldens; CI fails when goldens change without that variable.
The suite runs headless on macOS CI in under 3 minutes with no window server permission prompts.
notes: Frozen clock and fixed fonts are required for determinism; disable animations in test builds.

title: CLI command tree and global flags
description: `at-cli` binary `agentuna` with clap. TU owns the top-level commands `projects`, `scan`, `doctor`, `completions` and `version`. The binary also registers noun-first domain groups as extension points: `skills`, `mcp`, `mcp secret`, `migrate`, `adopt`, `drift`, `backups`, `sync`, `remote`, `agents`, `effective`, `why`, `overview` and `rules`. Each group is contributed by its owning slice through a `CommandGroup` trait and attaches its own subcommands; at-cli adds no domain logic. Global flags `--json`, `--project <path>`, `--scope`, `--yes`, `--verbose`, `--no-color`.
acceptance: `agentuna --help` lists the TU-owned commands `projects`, `scan`, `doctor`, `completions`, `version` and every registered domain group name from the list above.
The composition root registers only implemented groups, so the binary compiles and `--help` lists exactly the registered groups plus TU-owned commands; an unregistered group is absent, not a stub.
Unknown subcommand, unknown flag or missing required argument exits 2 with usage on stderr.
Global flags parse before and after the subcommand; `--json` is accepted everywhere.
`completions zsh|bash` emits scripts accepted by `zsh -n` and `bash -n`.
notes: Group ownership per integrator decision: skills -> TS-041, mcp and mcp secret -> TM-027, migrate/adopt/drift/backups/sync/remote -> TC-030/TC-031, agents/effective/why/overview/rules -> TA-070/TA-071. TU owns only the tree, projects, scan, doctor, completions and version; groups attach through the CommandGroup trait.

title: CLI projects and scan commands
description: TU-owned read and registry commands: `projects list|add|remove|use` and `scan`. `projects list` shows registered projects with path, counts and last used; `add` registers a folder, `remove` hides it and `use` makes it active. `scan` walks configured roots (default `~/Projects` plus user-added folders) with `--depth` and reports discovered, new, missing and unchanged sets. Both support `--json` and build output through the TU-033 envelope.
acceptance: `projects list --json` matches the golden schema with name, path, counts, last_used_at and hidden flag; ordering is last_used_at desc then name.

`projects add <path>` registers a folder and returns its id; adding an already registered path, including through a symlink, selects the existing row, exits 0 and emits an `already_registered` warning.
`projects remove <path>` hides the project without deleting deployments or history; `projects use <path>` updates last_used_at and the active project.
`scan --json` returns discovered, new, missing and unchanged sets plus warnings for permission-denied roots; it never writes into agent folders and exits 0 when only warnings are present.
With `--json`, stdout holds exactly one JSON object and all logs go to stderr.
notes: Registry and scan behaviour are owned by TU-011 and TU-012; this story is the CLI surface.

title: CLI doctor command
description: `doctor [--fix] [--json]` checks store path writability, SQLite integrity and schema version, agent path readability, Keychain access, free disk space, watcher start and binary version. Each finding carries severity, code, message and suggested fix.
acceptance: Every check emits a finding with severity ok/warn/error, a stable code, message and fix hint; JSON puts them under `data.findings`.
Any error finding exits 8; a warnings-only run exits 0 with `ok: true` and warnings populated.
A permission-denied agent folder is reported as an error naming the path but does not crash the run.
`--fix` performs only safe repairs (create store directories, rebuild index) and lists each action taken.
notes: Doctor is also the support entry point linked from SKILL.md.

title: CLI JSON schema and exit code contract
description: Document and enforce the machine contract used by agents and every command group: `schema_version: 1`, envelope `{schema_version, command, ok, data, warnings, error}`, error object `{code, message, details, hint}` and the exit code table (0 success, 2 usage, 3 parse/validation, 4 not found, 5 locked, 6 conflict/native/concurrent write, 7 partial, 8 doctor failure, 9 confirmation required, 10 network required/offline). TU-033 is the single owner: the TU commands `projects`, `scan`, `doctor`, `completions` and every registered domain group (`skills`, `mcp`, `mcp secret`, `migrate`, `adopt`, `drift`, `backups`, `sync`, `remote`, `agents`, `effective`, `why`, `overview`, `rules`) must build output through the shared envelope and exit-code helper.
acceptance: Every command returns one of the documented exit codes; a golden test invokes each code path and asserts it.
JSON mode writes exactly one parseable object to stdout and only diagnostics to stderr.
Every error object has a stable machine code and a non-empty hint; codes are frozen by test.
Adding a field is allowed within schema_version 1; removing or renaming a field requires schema_version 2 and the test fails otherwise.
A contract test iterates every registered command group and asserts its `--help` and a smoke invocation go through the shared envelope helper and return a documented exit code.
notes: The contract is mirrored in the SKILL.md from TU-037.

title: CLI uses the same engine as the app
description: Guard the architectural rule that the CLI is a thin front end: at-cli may depend only on at-model, at-store, at-engine, at-adapters, at-migrate, at-fs and at-db; it must not write agent files or open SQLite directly. Same intent must produce the same ChangeSet from CLI and UI.
acceptance: A dependency test fails if at-cli adds rusqlite, direct std/fs writes or a new IO crate.
For the same fixture store and intent, CLI `--dry-run` and the UI planner produce byte-identical serialized ChangeSets.
CLI writes go through at-fs safe write with backup and concurrency checks; a test asserts a backup exists after a mutating command such as `skills enable`.
CLI operations carry the same actor, timestamp and source fields as UI operations in the `operations` table.
notes: Test-layer architecture guard, not a feature.

title: live UI refresh when CLI changes files
description: The app subscribes to at-fs watcher events and reloads affected entities when a CLI run or an agent rewrites a file. Debounce and coalesce bursts, suppress AgenTuna's own writes by operation id and content hash, and protect dirty editors with a `Changed outside AgenTuna` banner.
acceptance: With the app open, `agentuna skills enable X --agent codex --scope user` updates the Skills table within 500 ms after the debounce, without Rescan.
A burst of 200 file events produces at most 3 reload batches, measured in a test with a synthetic event source.
AgenTuna's own writes never retrigger a reload loop, asserted by an event-count test around a single apply.
A dirty editor shows a banner with Reload and Keep mine; Reload confirms and discards, Keep mine leaves both versions and marks drift.
Deleting a store file closes its detail screen and shows an error state instead of panicking.
notes: The watcher itself is TF-007; this story owns UI reaction and loop suppression.

title: packaged CLI install to PATH
description: Ship `agentuna` inside the .app bundle Resources and expose `Help > Install Command Line Tool`. Install a symlink into /usr/local/bin when writable, else offer ~/.local/bin, print the PATH export line and an uninstall action. Never overwrite a foreign file.
acceptance: Install creates a symlink pointing at the bundled binary and reports the resolved path; `which agentuna` works in a fresh login shell.
An existing non-symlink at the target path is never overwritten; the dialog names the path and offers another location.
When /usr/local/bin is not writable, the dialog offers ~/.local/bin and prints the exact export line to add to the shell profile.
Uninstall removes the symlink only when it resolves to this app's bundled binary; a foreign symlink is left alone with a warning.
The installed tool reports the same version string as the app.
notes: Signing and notarization are release-pipeline work; this story covers bundling and the symlink flow.

title: SKILL.md that teaches agents the CLI
description: Author `skills/agentuna/SKILL.md` with saphyr frontmatter (name, description) and an agent-facing guide for the noun-first CLI: `projects list`, `scan`, `effective`, `why`, `skills list|enable|disable|install`, `mcp list|add`, `mcp secret`, `rules`, `migrate scan|plan|apply|undo`, `backups create|list|restore`, `doctor`. JSON usage with jq examples, exit code table and safety rules. Shipped in the repo and installable with `npx skills add <owner>/<repo>`.
acceptance: Frontmatter parses with saphyr and contains name and description; the file is under 400 lines.
Every `agentuna ...` command shown in a fenced block resolves in `agentuna --help`, including group subcommands; a test parses the file and asserts this.

The guide documents `--json`, the envelope and exit code table, and rules: dry-run before writes, never edit agent files directly, ask before `migrate apply` or `backups restore`, never print secret values.
Install line uses `npx skills add <owner>/<repo>` with the release repository substituted; the file contains no credentials and no absolute home paths.
A troubleshooting section points to `agentuna doctor --json` and `why` for state inspection.
notes: The skill is documentation plus fixtures; no runtime code.

title: CLI integration tests over a fake HOME
description: Spawn the real `agentuna` binary against the TF-010 temp HOME fixture and assert exit codes, JSON envelopes and filesystem effects for the TU commands (`projects`, `scan`, `doctor`, `completions`) and for every registered domain group by name: `skills`, `mcp`, `mcp secret`, `migrate`, `adopt`, `drift`, `backups`, `sync`, `remote`, `agents`, `effective`, `why`, `overview`, `rules`. Cover malformed files, a permission-denied agent folder, native conflict, concurrent external write and offline git install.
acceptance: At least 15 cases cover `projects list|add|remove|use`, `scan`, `doctor`, `completions` and one smoke invocation per registered group, in both `--json` and human modes.
Failure fixtures assert exact exit codes and `error.code` values from TU-033.
Each case hashes the fixture tree before and after and fails on any unexpected file change.
The suite runs in under 60 seconds on CI, requires no network, and is deterministic across repeated runs.

title: project picker and palette search tests
description: Unit and interaction tests for project filtering, search-span highlighting, fuzzy ranking, keyboard navigation and deep-link resolution. Testing Library user events drive the picker and palette without a window.
acceptance: Ranking fixtures assert order for exact prefix, word-boundary, subsequence and no-match queries over 10,000 entries.
Highlight spans are asserted for name and path matches, including two matches in one path.
Keyboard sequences Up/Down/Enter/Esc/Cmd+Enter assert focus and resulting route; Esc never changes the route.
Filtering 2,000 projects stays under 16 ms and palette search stays under 8 ms in the test bench.
Deep links map item ids to routes; unknown ids produce the not-found toast and preserve the previous route.

title: scope switcher widget
description: `ui/src/components/scope_switcher` is a presentational segmented control for Global / User / Project, with a fourth Local segment shown only when the active project enables Local. It receives the current scope and returns a `ScopeSelected` event; it owns no scope state, routing or persistence (TA-053 owns those). States: normal, active, disabled, locked, Local hidden.
acceptance: Renders Global, User and Project; Local renders only when the active project enables it, using the label `Local (only you, this repo)`.
States normal, active, disabled with reason `Choose a project first`, locked Global and Local hidden each render without layout shift at 1x and 2x.
The widget is purely presentational: it takes the current scope and emits exactly one `ScopeSelected` event per click or keyboard activation; it stores no state and persists nothing.
ARIA exposes role, label `Scope`, selected segment and disabled reason; segments are reachable with Tab and arrow keys.
Snapshot coverage includes all five states in dark and light themes.
notes: Scope state, routing and persistence are owned by TA-053. Scope shortcuts are Cmd+Shift+1/2/3/4 and are owned by TU-016.

title: Add menu
description: `ui/src/overlays/menus` implements the Add menu from the top bar: New skill, Add MCP server, New rule file. Each routes into the relevant flow in the active scope and closes the menu.
acceptance: Cmd+N and the Add button open the menu; Up/Down/Enter activate and Esc closes.
Each item routes to its flow with the active scope preselected and the menu closes.
Items are disabled with a reason when the scope is read-only or a required agent is missing.
Menu closes on route change and restores focus to the Add button.

title: Account menu
description: `ui/src/overlays/menus` implements the account block menu: Preferences, Backups & restore, Keychain secrets, Agents on this Mac, About. It states `No account, no telemetry` and shows the app version.
acceptance: Every item routes or opens its dialog; the menu closes on selection.
The menu shows `No account, no telemetry` and the version; no sign-in or account control exists.
Items are disabled with a reason when unavailable, for example Backups during an active migration.
Keyboard reachable with the same navigation rules as TU-004; closes on route change and restores focus.

title: network action gate and offline states
description: `ui/src/components` renders network policy state supplied by TF-036 (`NetworkAction` registry in at-model): per-action available, blocked or confirmation-required state, offline labelling, first-use confirmation and network entries in the operations log. TU-043 does not define, register or extend actions; it reads TF-036 and renders exactly what the policy returns.
acceptance: Every network-capable action shown in the UI gets its state and reason from TF-036; at-app contains no second action list, and a test injects a stub registry and asserts the rendered set matches it.
When TF-036 marks an action confirmation-required, the UI renders a confirmation naming the destination host; Cancel leaves state untouched and records nothing.
Offline mode or detected offline state renders the `Offline` label and the TF-036 reason, and policy changes re-render without restart.
A scheduled HTTP health check renders as blocked while `background_health=local` and as allowed when `background_health=all`, driven only by TF-036 state.
Network actions surface the `network` flag and destination host from the operation record; no telemetry or analytics call exists.
notes: Engine and adapter enforcement lives in the owning slices; this story owns the registry, UI gating and offline presentation.
